title: Literature repair list and question-level analysis
subject: English Literature
unit: Spring 2: Masterclass and Component 1: anthology, unseen poetry and Of Mice and Men
source: Seeded from english-literature/y11 lessons 35, 45 (Literature repair list and question-level analysis (pupil PDF))
intro: Answer every question. Show your working. Mark it with the mark scheme and log any errors in your repair list.

questions.q: in the portal response box, rewrite your weakest mock paragraph so it meets its section's AO weighting. Starter: 'Priestley presents...' or 'Shakespeare presents...'
questions.a: A repaired paragraph with argument (AO1), close analysis (AO2) and, for Macbeth, context (AO4).
questions.model: AIC before: 'Mr Birling sacks Eva and is selfish.' After: 'Priestley presents Mr Birling as the voice of selfish capitalism: his claim that "a man has to mind his own business and look after himself and his own" is immediately undercut by the Inspector's arrival, so the structure itself rejects his view.'

questions.q: add your Literature repairs to the repair list with dates.
write one sentence of context for An Inspector Calls that explains, not decorates.
questions.a: For example: Writing in 1945, Priestley wanted audiences to build a fairer society after two world wars.

questions.q: Fill in your mock analysis and circle your two biggest losses.
questions.a: Marks recorded; two losses with causes.
questions.model: Teacher models with an anonymous paper: 'Section B Macbeth 14/30: no AO4. Section A AIC 18/30: plot retold. Biggest gains: Macbeth context, AIC analysis.'

questions.q: Name the cause of each loss.
Answer the ponder in one sentence.
questions.a: Answers vary; it helps only if you know where key scenes are before the exam.

questions.q: in the portal response box, repair one paragraph from your weakest section using the model. Starter: '[Writer] presents...'
questions.a: An improved paragraph meeting the section's AO weighting.
questions.model: Unseen before: 'The poem is sad and has a worm.' After: 'The poet turns grief towards renewal at the word "Still": the worm, "curled like a question", carries on "the work of spring", so life continues even as the final line names the loss plainly.'

questions.q: write your dated revision plan to 12 and 19 May (portal).
questions.a: A weekly plan with timed tasks and retrieval.

questions.q: write a ten-question retrieval quiz on your weakest text for a partner.
Compare your timed answers with the labelled models; list two gaps.
questions.model: Teacher models: 'My Macbeth answer: strong AO2, no AO4 in paragraphs 2 and 3. My unseen: good images, no structure.'

questions.q: How ready are you for the Literature exams?
